subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Handy's 'role culture' is typically associated with:
options: A bureaucratic organisation with clear job roles, rules and hierarchy
A loose network of independent specialists
A flexible, project-based structure
An entrepreneur making all decisions personally
questions.explain: A role culture is bureaucratic, relying on defined roles, procedures and a clear hierarchy.

questions.q: A direct tax differs from an indirect tax in that a direct tax is:
options: Collected by retailers on the government's behalf
Always paid by businesses only
Levied directly on income or profits
Levied on spending, such as VAT
questions.explain: Direct taxes (e.g. income tax, corporation tax) are charged on income or profit, unlike indirect taxes on spending.

questions.q: A SWOT analysis would classify a new free-trade agreement opening up an export market as a:
options: Weakness
Opportunity
Strength
Threat
questions.explain: A favourable external development such as a new export market is an opportunity in SWOT.

questions.q: Kotter and Schlesinger suggest that 'manipulation and co-optation' as a way of handling resistance is:
options: The slowest but most ethical approach
Identical to participation and involvement
A fast approach that can lead to future problems if people feel manipulated
Only suitable when there is no time pressure
questions.explain: Manipulation and co-optation can be quick and cheap but risks resentment and loss of trust if discovered.

questions.q: A common cause of resistance to change among employees is:
options: A strong desire for more uncertainty
Fear of the unknown and concern over job security
Excessive confidence that change will benefit them
An eagerness to lose established routines
questions.explain: People often resist change because of fear of the unknown and worries about their jobs and status.

questions.q: Competition law is designed mainly to:
options: Fix minimum prices across markets
Guarantee profits for large firms
Prevent anti-competitive practices and protect consumer interests
Encourage firms to form cartels
questions.explain: Competition law prohibits practices like price-fixing and abuse of market power to protect competition and consumers.

questions.q: Buyer (customer) bargaining power in Porter's model tends to be highest when:
options: The product is essential and has no alternatives
There are few buyers each purchasing large volumes and products are undifferentiated
There are many small buyers and products are highly differentiated
Switching costs for buyers are extremely high
questions.explain: A small number of large buyers facing standardised products can demand lower prices, giving them strong bargaining power.

questions.q: A limitation of relying heavily on data for decision-making is that:
options: Data is always completely objective and certain
Data can never be quantified
Past data may not reliably predict future conditions
It removes all need for managerial judgement
questions.explain: Historical data may not hold in a changing environment, so it cannot replace managerial judgement.

questions.q: A fall in a country's exchange rate (a weaker currency) tends to:
options: Have no effect on trade
Reduce the cost of imported raw materials
Make exports more price-competitive and imports more expensive
Make imports cheaper and exports dearer
questions.explain: A weaker currency lowers the foreign price of exports (more competitive) and raises import prices.

questions.q: Net present value (NPV) appraisal is superior to payback because it:
options: Accounts for the time value of money by discounting future cash flows
Is always quicker to calculate
Ignores the timing of cash flows
Requires no estimate of future cash flows
questions.explain: NPV discounts future cash flows to present value, recognising that money now is worth more than later.

questions.q: Organisational culture can act as a barrier to change because:
options: It only affects junior staff, never managers
It has no influence on employee behaviour
Deeply held values and 'the way we do things here' may conflict with new methods
Cultures change instantly when leaders demand it
questions.explain: An entrenched culture embodies shared assumptions that can clash with and resist new strategies.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the difference between strategy and tactics?
options: Strategy is short-term and reactive; tactics are long-term and planned
Strategy and tactics are interchangeable terms for the same plans
Strategy sets long-term direction to achieve overall objectives; tactics are the shorter-term actions used to implement it
Tactics are decided by senior managers; strategy is decided by junior staff
questions.explain: Strategy is the long-term plan for achieving objectives, while tactics are the day-to-day or short-term actions that carry the strategy out.

questions.q: A firm sells its existing products to a new overseas market for the first time. On Ansoff's matrix this is:
options: Market development
Market penetration
Diversification
Product development
questions.explain: Selling existing products to new markets is market development.

questions.q: A key limitation of using decision trees is that:
options: They can only be used for HR decisions
They ignore the cost of each decision
The probabilities used are often estimates that may be inaccurate
They cannot show different options at once
questions.explain: Decision trees rely on estimated probabilities and values, which may be subjective or wrong.

questions.q: In a competitive (fragmented) market with many similar firms, competitive rivalry is usually:
options: Determined only by suppliers
Low, allowing high prices
High, putting downward pressure on prices
Eliminated entirely
questions.explain: Many similar competitors intensify rivalry, typically driving prices and margins down.

questions.q: Fiscal policy refers to the government's use of:
options: Interest rates and the money supply
Trade tariffs only
Taxation and government spending
Exchange rate controls
questions.explain: Fiscal policy uses taxation and government spending to influence the economy.

questions.q: In the Boston Matrix, a 'problem child' (question mark) is characterised by:
options: Low market share, high market growth
High market share, low market growth
Low market share, low market growth
High market share, high market growth
questions.explain: Problem children have low share in fast-growing markets and need heavy investment to develop.

questions.q: Consumer protection legislation primarily aims to:
options: Prevent firms from merging
Limit the wages firms can pay
Protect customers from being misled or sold unsafe goods
Set the level of corporation tax
questions.explain: Consumer law protects buyers, requiring goods to be safe, as described and fit for purpose.

questions.q: GDP is best defined as:
options: The total amount of money in circulation
The government's annual budget
The value of a country's exports only
The total value of goods and services produced in an economy in a period
questions.explain: GDP measures the total value of output produced within an economy over a given period.

questions.q: In Porter's value chain, which of the following is a primary activity rather than a support activity?
options: Technology development
Human resource management
Firm infrastructure
Outbound logistics
questions.explain: Outbound logistics is one of the five primary activities; HRM, technology development and infrastructure are support activities.

questions.q: In Charles Handy's classification, a 'power culture' is one in which:
options: Control radiates from a central figure or small group with few rules
Individuals work as autonomous experts with little hierarchy
Authority is spread evenly across self-managing teams
Roles and procedures are rigidly defined by bureaucracy
questions.explain: A power culture centres control on a dominant individual or core group, with decisions made centrally and few formal rules.

questions.q: According to Ansoff's matrix, the strategy of launching a new product into a new market is:
options: Diversification, the highest risk
Market penetration, the lowest risk
Product development, a moderate risk
Market development, a moderate risk
questions.explain: Diversification means new product plus new market and is the riskiest quadrant of Ansoff's matrix.

questions.q: During a recession, a business is most likely to face:
options: Falling demand and increased pressure on cash flow
Severe shortages of labour
Rapidly rising prices from excess demand
Rising consumer demand and confidence
questions.explain: A recession brings falling demand and lower confidence, straining sales and cash flow.

questions.q: A PESTLE analysis examines all of the following EXCEPT:
options: Political and legal factors
Internal financial ratios of the firm
Economic and social factors
Technological and environmental factors
questions.explain: PESTLE covers external Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors, not internal finance.

questions.q: A rise in interest rates is most likely to:
options: Encourage borrowing and increase consumer spending
Reduce the cost of servicing existing variable-rate debt
Discourage borrowing and reduce consumer spending
Have no impact on firms with loans
questions.explain: Higher interest rates raise borrowing costs, dampening spending and investment.

questions.q: A decision has two outcomes: a 0.6 chance of £100,000 and a 0.4 chance of £50,000. Its expected value is:
Inflation is best defined as:
options: A fall in the value of exports
A one-off rise in the price of a single good
A sustained rise in the general price level
An increase in real output
questions.explain: Inflation is a sustained increase in the average price level across the economy.

questions.q: Offshoring differs from outsourcing because offshoring specifically means:
options: Using a third party in the same country
Importing finished goods from abroad
Selling a subsidiary to a foreign buyer
Relocating a business activity to another country (whether kept in-house or not)
questions.explain: Offshoring is relocating an activity abroad; it can be done in-house and is therefore distinct from outsourcing.

questions.q: The payback period method of investment appraisal measures:
options: The present value of future cash flows
The percentage return per year on the investment
The total profit an investment will generate
The time taken for an investment to recover its initial cost
questions.explain: Payback measures how long it takes for net cash inflows to repay the initial outlay.

questions.q: In Porter's five forces, which factor is NOT one of the five?
options: The level of corporation tax
The bargaining power of suppliers
The threat of new entrants
Competitive rivalry
questions.explain: Porter's five forces are new entrants, supplier power, buyer power, substitutes and rivalry — tax is not one.
